title: Palbociclib with endocrine therapy
context_label: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
schedule_label: Oral treatment with a planned rest week
schedule_summary: The usual palbociclib starting dose is 125 mg once daily; a lower dose may be prescribed. Palbociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, then paused on Days 22–28 of each 28-day cycle. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily, or fulvestrant follows its injection schedule. Ovarian suppression has its own plan when required.
purpose: Palbociclib slows cell-cycle progression while the hormone partner reduces oestrogen signalling. The aim in this advanced-disease pathway is cancer control, with treatment and response reviewed over time.
indication_text: HR-positive/HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic disease with an AI, or with fulvestrant after previous endocrine therapy as defined in NCCP. Pre/perimenopausal endocrine treatment requires ovarian suppression; the exact partner and its risks must be confirmed.
administration_text: Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. Avoid grapefruit. If you miss or vomit a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Do not restart after a clinical hold until the treating team confirms.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile. Confirm receptor status, exact endocrine partner, previous endocrine therapy, menopause/ovarian suppression, pregnancy precautions and interacting medicines. FBC on Day 1 and Day 15 of cycles 1–2; Day 1 from cycle 3 and extra checks as indicated. Only after at most grade 1–2 neutropenia throughout the first six cycles may FBC monitoring reduce to every three months, before the start of a cycle and as indicated. Renal and liver profile before each cycle; review fever/infection, mouth/bowel symptoms, fatigue, pulmonary symptoms and adherence. No routine palbociclib-specific Day-14 ECG or echo timetable; investigate when clinically indicated.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Palbociclib
agents.mechanism: Blocks cell-cycle signals that help cancer cells divide
agents.explanation: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division.
agents.watch: The key early issue is a falling white-cell count, which may cause no symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report infection symptoms or new cough/breathlessness promptly.
risks: Rare but serious interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis

agents.name: Your endocrine partner
agents.type: Either an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant
agents.mechanism: Reduces oestrogen signalling to hormone-sensitive cells
visual: AI lowers oestrogen; fulvestrant targets its receptor
agents.explanation: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant acts at the oestrogen receptor. These are alternative partners here, not an instruction to take both. The partner’s dose, monitoring and injection or tablet schedule must be confirmed.
agents.watch: Discuss joint/hot-flush and bone symptoms with an AI, or injection-site/bleeding symptoms with fulvestrant. Pre/perimenopausal women require ovarian suppression in the prescribed combination.
risks: Hot flushes and other hormone-related symptoms
AI: joint symptoms and bone loss
Partner-specific liver, interaction and pregnancy considerations

urgent_extra: Contact the treatment team promptly if you feel feverish or unwell, have shaking chills or infection symptoms, or develop new cough or breathlessness. Follow the local emergency temperature instructions; do not wait for a planned blood test or for the 38.5°C value used in one clinician dose-adjustment table. Severe breathing difficulty needs emergency care.

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the exact medicine, strength, endocrine partner, baseline tests and first review appointments. Ask who arranges tests and who reviews the results.

sections.title: Taking treatment
sections.text: Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. Avoid grapefruit. If you miss or vomit a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Do not restart after a clinical hold until the treating team confirms.

sections.title: Your endocrine partner has a separate timetable
sections.text: An aromatase inhibitor is normally taken daily through the targeted-medicine rest week. If fulvestrant is the chosen partner, the usual schedule is 500 mg by intramuscular injection on Days 1, 15 and 29, then once monthly; confirm the prescribed dose and appointment dates. Any ovarian-suppression injections have their own schedule.

sections.title: Treatment duration
sections.text: Repeat while beneficial and tolerated. The planned week off concerns palbociclib, not automatically the endocrine partner.

sections.title: Supply and appointments
sections.text: Request the next supply before tablets run out. Blood tests and any ECG or injections need their own appointments. This oral treatment does not itself require a central line or infusion pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask which medicine is held, whether the endocrine partner continues, what needs to recover, when the next review is due and who will authorise restart.

sections.title: Support between appointments
sections.text: Keep the oncology contact details and prescribed symptom medicines accessible. New severe symptoms need prompt assessment rather than waiting for the next blood test.

evidence.title: PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3: keep endocrine partner and analysis separate
evidence.intro: Studies describe groups. Ask how closely the treatment and study population match your situation.
evidence.population: PALOMA-2: 666 postmenopausal women with ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced disease and no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease. PALOMA-3: 521 women with progression or relapse during prior endocrine therapy.
evidence.interpretation: Palbociclib with hormone therapy can delay cancer growth. Studies used different hormone partners and different prior-treatment groups. The final overall trial results did not establish a clear survival improvement with palbociclib; later exploratory follow-up needs to be interpreted separately.
evidence.limitations: Your team can discuss the strength and limitations of the evidence alongside treatment risks and alternatives.

teachback: Which medicine is taken when, which test is due next, who reviews it, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, benefit and uncertainty, important medicine-specific risks, reproductive precautions, symptom support and planned duration. Confirm the endocrine partner and any ovarian-suppression plan. The timeline does not authorise a restart or certify clinical review.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: Palbociclib is oral minimal–low emetic risk. Premedication is not usually required; agree rescue treatment if symptoms occur.

support.title: Blood counts and infection
support.text: Attend early and pre-cycle blood tests. Dose holds and reductions are clinician decisions. Growth-factor injections are not a routine automatic prescription for every patient.

support.title: Endocrine-partner support
support.text: Agree help for hot flushes, joints, vaginal or sexual symptoms, sleep and bone health. Fulvestrant injection discomfort and any ovarian-suppression injections have separate support plans.

support.title: Formulation and interactions
support.text: Check whether the pack contains capsules or tablets and follow the food instructions for that product. Check new medicines, supplements and grapefruit interactions.

support.title: Symptoms between visits
support.text: Report mouth ulcers, persistent bowel symptoms, worsening fatigue, fever or new breathing symptoms promptly.

timeline.label: Palbociclib rest week
timeline.text: No palbociclib; next cycle only after team confirmation

timeline.label: Endocrine partner
timeline.text: AI every day OR fulvestrant at its scheduled injection visits

timeline.label: Blood-count changes
timeline.text: May occur without symptoms. FBC Day 1 and Day 15 of first 2 cycles; extra tests if low.

timeline.label: Symptoms vary between people
timeline.text: Mouth soreness, nausea or fatigue can occur; no guaranteed day-by-day prediction.

timeline_note: Treatment days are specified by the regimen. Symptom timing varies; the full-cycle symptom bands show that an effect can occur at any point, not a measured probability or severity.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment and rest
chronology_notes.text: Take palbociclib for 21 days, then have 7 days without palbociclib. The aromatase-inhibitor tablet continues every day, or fulvestrant injections follow their separate schedule. The week off applies to palbociclib, not automatically to the hormone treatment.

chronology_notes.title: Tests and appointments
chronology_notes.text: Use the monitoring table for baseline and later checks. A rest week does not remove infection or other risks.

safety_note: Contact the treatment team promptly if you feel feverish or unwell, have shaking chills or infection symptoms, or develop new cough or breathlessness. Follow the local emergency temperature instructions; do not wait for a planned blood test or for the 38.5°C value used in one clinician dose-adjustment table. Severe breathing difficulty needs emergency care.

chapters.title: What the studies tell us
chapters.intro: Palbociclib with hormone therapy can delay cancer growth. Studies used different hormone partners and different prior-treatment groups. The final overall trial results did not establish a clear survival improvement with palbociclib; later exploratory follow-up needs to be interpreted separately.

items.title: How to interpret this
items.text: Study results describe groups with defined treatment and eligibility. Ask about your own likely benefits, important harms, alternatives and remaining uncertainty.

items.text: The team confirms the plan for each medicine and the next review. Do not restart a clinically held treatment from this educational timeline.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates?
questions.a: No. This map shows general timing without personal information. Your hospital arranges actual appointments; ask who books each test and who reviews its result.

questions.q: What if a dose is missed or treatment is held?
questions.a: Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. Avoid grapefruit. If you miss or vomit a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Do not restart after a clinical hold until the treating team confirms. A hold may affect one medicine rather than the whole combination; confirm each component.

questions.q: What happens after treatment changes or ends?
questions.a: Repeat while beneficial and tolerated. The planned week off concerns palbociclib, not automatically the endocrine partner. Keep the separately agreed disease follow-up, endocrine and bone-health plan.
